catalog_quote: Takayama Michiaki (1981, 1982, 1983, 1984) has demonstrated statistical correlations between the Middle Japanese accent recorded in the Myôgishô (1081 CE) and the Middle Chinese tones of the phonograms of poems in the parts of Shoki which Mori (1991: 138) calls the 'alpha' section. The Chinese Level Tone corresponds to Japanese low pitch, and the Chinese 'oblique' tones (Rising, Departing, and Entering) correspond to Japanese high pitch ... From this evidence it would appear that OJ accent was not much different from that of Middle Japanese accent (Mori 1991: 138). ... Even within poems written with apparent accentual notation, there are mismatches between phonogram tones and the expected pitches of OJ syllables. ... I will conclude my discussion of this issue here because I do not intend to reconstruct OJ accent in this book. However, I will note that no other transcriptions of Japanes…

tone_statements.citation: Hayata, Teruhiro. 2024. Reconstruction of Old Japanese phonology. In: Handbook of Historical Japanese Linguistics (Handbooks of Japanese Language and Linguistics; ed. B. Frellesvig, S. Kinsui et al.), ch. 4, pp. 101-132. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton.
tone_statements.quote: 以上のことから判断し、本稿の一応の結論を述べるならば、Ⅰ日本書紀音仮名表記部分の一部、ことに巻三、巻二十四〜巻二十七の歌謡においては、音仮名連続における原音声調の配置に、書紀述作時の日本語のアクセントが反映している可能性がある。Ⅱその表記部分においては、日本語の低平調の音節に原音声調が平声の調類に属する漢字を、高い部分を有する音節に原音声調が上声・去声の調類に属する漢字を宛てた可能性がある。 … いずれにせよ、現段階では「可能性」の指摘に踏みとどまらざるを得ないが、本稿に見た一応の結論は、今後へ向けての作業仮説としては有効かと思う。
tone_statements.translation: Judging from the above, the tentative conclusions of this paper are: I. In part of the phonogram-spelt portions of the Nihon shoki, especially the songs of vol. 3 and vols. 24-27, the arrangement of the original (Chinese) tones in the phonogram sequences possibly reflects the accent of Japanese at the time the Shoki was composed. II. In those portions, characters whose original tone belongs to the Level-tone class were possibly assigned to Japanese syllables of low level pitch, and characters of the Rising- or Departing-tone classes to syllables having a high part. ... At this stage one cannot go beyond pointing out the 'possibility', but this tentative conclusion should be valid as a working hypothesis.
tone_statements.locator: p.19, end of sec. 三 比較の結果 (conclusions Ⅰ-Ⅱ) (left half-lines) + 265-270, 278-280 (right half-lines)
tone_statements.summary: Old Japanese pitch accent may show in Nihon shoki (720) phonograms: low syllables get Chinese Level-tone graphs, those with a high part Rising/Departing ones; a hypothesis, no accent classes counted.

tone_statements.citation: Bentley, John R. 2001. A Descriptive Grammar of Early Old Japanese Prose. (Brill's Japanese Studies Library.) Leiden: Brill. Ch. 'Phonology', pp. 37-60.
tone_statements.quote: なお︑上代のアクセントについては︑中古末期のアクセント体系と大きく違わなかっただろうと推定されているので︑小論もそれに従って︑中古のアクセント資料から上代の脱落形における両形態素のアクセントを推定した上で︑考察を行う︒ … (0は低平調︑●は高平調︶ … (9は上昇調︑ C は下降調︶ … 曲調音節は現れる位置や語に偏りがあり︑語中に現れることは極めて少ない︒ … 脱落形の多くはアクセントの面でもひとまとまりであり︑高音部がニヶ所以上に分かれる場合は極めて少ない︒ … 上代と中古が同じアクセント体系下にあったとみなし得ることも確認できた︒
tone_statements.translation: As for Old Japanese accent, it is presumed not to have differed greatly from the accent system of the late Early Middle Japanese period, so this paper follows that view and infers the accent of both morphemes in the OJ deleted forms from the EMJ accent materials before proceeding. … (○ = low level tone, ● = high level tone) … (9 = rising tone, C = falling tone) … contour-tone syllables are skewed as to position and word and very rarely occur word-internally. … most deleted forms are a single unit in accent as well, and cases where the high-pitched portion is split into two or more places are extremely rare. … it could also be confirmed that OJ and EMJ may be regarded as having been under the same accent system.
tone_statements.locator: p.36 end of はじめに; p.37; p.45 四・一; p.47 五 おわりに; n.10 下降調 = 上声の一変種 (l.860-864) and n.15 (l.911-918)
tone_statements.summary: Old Japanese assumed to share the late Early Middle Japanese accent system: each syllable high or low level pitch, usually one high stretch per word; rising/falling syllables rare; stress not treated.

tone_statements.citation: 奥村三雄 [Okumura Mitsuo]. 1993. 上代語アクセント小考 [A note on Old Japanese accent]. 訓点語と訓点資料 (訓点語学会) 90: 48-60.
tone_statements.quote: 同じα群でも巻廿四〜廿六のものに限って見るならば … 各類の分布差はかなりはっきりしてくるのである(表Ⅲ)。すなわち、第一類名詞(①)は《上—非平》の欄、第二類名詞(②)は《上—平》の欄、第三類名詞(③)は《平—平》の欄、第四類名詞(④)は《平—非平》の欄に、といった具合である。 … 『類聚名義抄』における二音節名詞各類への差声が、原則として 第一類22 第二類21 第三類11 第四類12 第五類11・12・1f〔いわゆる平声点・上声点・平声軽点を … 仮りに1・2・fと記す〕 … 筆者はかつて、巻三及び巻廿四〜廿六の音仮名表記において、原音声調の調類と後世の書紀古写本における声点の加点状況に、〈原音声調平声——1声点／同 非平声——非1声点〉の如き“対応”が、傾向として看取されることを指摘した。そこから、それらの巻々の音仮名表記に書紀述作時の日本語のアクセントの反映が期待されるとの推論を得たのであるが、二音節名詞アクセント語類を通じての観察からも、ほぼ同様のことが言えそうに思われる。
tone_statements.translation: If, even within the α group, one looks only at the items of vols. 24-26 … the distributional differences between the classes become quite clear (Table III): class-1 nouns (①) fall in the 《MC rising – non-level》 cell, class-2 nouns (②) in 《rising – level》, class-3 nouns (③) in 《level – level》, class-4 nouns (④) in 《level – non-level》. … In the Ruiju Myōgishō the tone-dot marking of the disyllabic-noun classes is in principle class 1 = 22, class 2 = 21, class 3 = 11, class 4 = 12, class 5 = 11/12/1f [the so-called level-tone dot, rising-tone dot and light level-tone dot are … provisionally written 1, 2, f] … The author once pointed out that in the phonogram spellings of vol. 3 and vols. 24-26 a 'correspondence' of the type 〈MC level tone — 1 dot / MC non-level tone — non-1 dot〉 can be observed, as a tendency, between the MC tone classes and the tone dots added in the later old manuscripts of the Shoki, and inferred from it that the phonogram spellings of those volumes may be expected to reflect the accent of Japanese at the time the Shoki was composed; observation through the disyllabic-noun accent classes seems to allow much the same to be said.
tone_statements.locator: p. 54 (upper register, end; lower register after Table III) running on to p. 55 upper register, before the ○ break
tone_statements.summary: Pitch accent: MC tones of Shoki α-group phonograms (vols 24-26) tend to reflect syllable pitch, level ~ low dot 1, non-level ~ high dot 2; noun classes 1-4 pattern 22, 21, 11, 12 as in the Myōgishō.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both the deciding quotation (pp. 37-39, PDF 56-58) and the domain quotation (p. 25, PDF 44) are verbatim in the Miyake 2003 PDF we hold/txt at the stated locators. (2) Deciding source: a 2003 phonology monograph (phonetic reconstruction of OJ) that reviews the only primary evidence for OJ prosody — Takayama's Shoki phonogram-tone / Myogisho pitch correlation — and concludes OJ had a pitch accent close to EMJ's, explicitly with no reconstruction and no stress statement. For an extinct philological language this is the appropriate evidence base; Glottolog's higher-ranked grammars (Vovin 2005/2020 WOJ; Kupchik 2011/2023 EOJ) cannot rest on different evidence, and the downloaded Kupchik 2011 confirms EOJ accent is simply 'unknown' (silent, consistent with no-stress coding).

sources.citation: 森博達 [Mori Hiromichi]. 2005. 日本書紀の万葉仮名と上代語のアクセント：日本書紀箚記(その4) [The man'yōgana of the Nihon shoki and the accent of Old Japanese: notes on the Nihon shoki 4]. 東アジアの古代文化 (古代学研究所編) 125: 117-129.
sources.note: Argues that some Nihon shoki phonogram spellings reflect Nara-period Japanese accent (Chinese level-tone graphs align with later low marks, oblique-tone graphs with high); no accent system is stated.

tone.quote: 平声の字には平声点,上声や去声のような仄声字には上声点が相対的に多いことが観察される。 … 書紀音仮名表記の一部において,音仮名連続における原音調類の配列と,同一語句の平安時代中央語のアクセントにある程度の相関性が見られることを指摘した。これら一部の音仮名表記は,平安時代語の前身である奈良時代中央語のアクセントを何らかの形で反映している可能性があると言えよう。以上が小論の結論である。そこからさらに踏み込んで,奈良時代中央語のアクセント体系に迫りたいところだが,これはかなり難しいと言わざるを得ない。
tone.locator: sec.3, p.20 + sec.5 言そ聞ゆる, p.28; quoted verbatim from dbtext l.43 and l.156-157
tone.translation: It is observed that level-tone characters relatively often carry the level-tone dot and oblique-tone characters, such as rising- or departing-tone ones, the rising-tone dot. … I have pointed out that in part of the Shoki phonogram spellings the sequence of original tone classes in phonogram strings correlates to some degree with the Heian-period central-Japanese accent of the same words. These spellings may reflect in some form the accent of Nara-period central Japanese, the predecessor of the Heian language. That is the conclusion of this paper. One would like to go further and approach the accent system of Nara-period central Japanese, but this must be called quite difficult.

tone.quote: 『日本書紀』α群音仮名の原音声調と平安時代京都アクセントとの対応状況について検討するための基礎資料を作成する。 … D : 原音声調による高低パターン(平声＝＿、上声・去声＝￣、入声＝△) E : 声点(L ＝平声、H ＝上声、R ＝去声、F ＝平声軽、△＝入声 鈴木豊(1988)(2003)による) F : 声点による推定アクセントの高低パターン(L ＝＿、H ＝￣、R ＝／、F ＝＼)
tone.locator: 要旨 p. 1 and 作業用資料・凡例 p. 4
tone.translation: [This paper] prepares groundwork data for examining how the original (Chinese) tones of the Nihon shoki alpha-group phonograms correspond to Heian-period Kyoto accent. … D: high/low pattern given by the original tones (level tone = ＿ [low], rising and departing tones = ￣ [high], entering tone = △); E: tone dots (L = 平声, H = 上声, R = 去声, F = 平声軽 'light level', △ = entering tone; after Suzuki 1988, 2003); F: high/low pattern of the accent inferred from the tone dots (L = ＿, H = ￣, R = ／ [rising], F = ＼ [falling]).

sources.note: Statistical study of the Middle Chinese tone classes of the Nihon Shoki song phonograms; assumes they may partly reflect Old Japanese accent of AD 720 but gives no accent or tone inventory.

tone.quote: 先に筆者は、日本書紀（A.D七二〇年撰）の音仮名を対象に、原音声調と日本語音との相関性を前提としてその機能的側面（＝日本語を表記するにあたっての）の模索を試みたことがある。 … また、筆者は先に、書紀音仮名表記の一部において原音声調が述作時のアクセントを反映している可能性のあることを指摘したが、それが巻三を除くとα群に多く見出されたことなど、あるいは何らかの関連を有するかも知れない。しかしいずれも憶測の域を出ない。 … 音仮名の原音と日本語音節との相関性を分析するにあたっては、suprasegmental な要素をも包括して把える視点が必要なのではないかと思う。
tone.locator: p.1, upper text block, 2nd paragraph; p.4, lower text block, end of section before the ○ break, with note (7); p.5, lower block, closing sentence just before 〔注〕; notes (2), (7), (11) on pp.5-6
tone.translation: Earlier the author, taking the ongana phonograms of the Nihon Shoki (compiled AD 720) as object, tried to explore their functional aspect (i.e. in writing Japanese) on the premise of a correlation between the original (Chinese) tones and the Japanese sounds. … Also, the author earlier pointed out the possibility that in part of the Shoki phonogram orthography the original tones reflect the accent of the time of composition; that this was found mostly in the alpha group (vol. 3 excepted) may perhaps be somehow related. But none of this goes beyond conjecture. … in analysing the correlation between the phonograms' original sounds and Japanese syllables, a viewpoint that also embraces suprasegmental elements seems to be needed.
